lines: gd8 stateful suite (devnet-8 state, BAL on, 341 tests, 6 CPUs = 3 cores, newPayload time): dbg d9466e629d (main + 8 open PRs: #25416 4x Ps, #25223, #25037, #25350, #25355, #25301, #25411, #25420) vs main f32a39d1e5: 7-8% less total time (0.920 / 0.931), geomean 0.97; all 341 tests pass. dbg no longer includes #25416
Slowest test, ether_transfers_onchain_receivers diff_to_contract: main 2.37 s (first run 3.18 s), dbg 1.23 s, about 1.9x
#25416 (GOMAXPROCS and page-fault-bound pools at 4x the CPUs): slowest test 1.8x in the suite; 3x Ps gives the same in the suite with eth_call 3.3% instead of 4.5% slower

#25452 (commitment reads from the shared state cache): within noise alone in this suite (2.5% faster on the slowest test with its pages cached), 1.31 to 1.21 s on the slowest test on top of #25416 (2x of main)

Within noise in the suite on #25416 + #25223 + #25339 + #25452: BAL commitment warmup off, 24 tip trie warmers instead of 3; but on the slowest test alone, cold, on #25416 the warmup is needed (all off 16% slower, commitment warmup off 9% slower). Slower: FILES_BLOCKING_ASYNC_IO 1.35x, also with 64 io_uring rings
Where the time goes on the slowest block: 215k reads of 4-8 KB, 4 in flight at 1x Ps and 11 at 4x; with the faults overlapped it is CPU-bound: commitment 1.7 CPU-s, sender recovery 0.7 CPU-s
Earlier, vs main 17822a558f: #25339 mem-batch shards vs main 17822a558f: 3.4% faster in total, ether_transfers 5.9% faster (26.0 to 23.7 s), account_access 1.4% faster

Within noise: self-loop workers exit after commit (0.8%), BranchCache skips an identical fill (0.9%), 3 trie BAL warmup workers instead of 6 (0%), code buffer kept across reader rebinds (0.1%), BAL read slots kept to the next block (0.6% on sstore/sload)

Slower: READ_AHEAD_BAL_CODE=true 51%; Gosched after each exec-loop publish 2.0% (ether_transfers 6.5%); state root computed ahead from the BAL for tip blocks 0.9% (ether_transfers 4.4%), its fold competes with exec for the 6 CPUs

Where the time goes: account_access runs serial cold CALLs, 21% of CPU reads code (decompress, then one cache copy); ether_transfers ends with a ~280 ms CPU-bound commitment fold after exec; sstore_bloated waits on I/O; ext_account_query_warm is EVM-bound
